summary: SOL-3: Base Aurora is a browser-based survival and learning game for ages 7–12, set at a fictional Mars outpost. Over three simulated sols, players lead a crew, complete missions that vary between runs, and balance power, oxygen, water, food, repairs, crop growth, communications, and radiation sheltering. Every major decision has a cost and changes the base, crew, or mission outcome, so players must weigh competing needs instead of choosing a free solution. Cinematic story scenes and AURA, an onboard companion, connect play to short science explanations. The game uses NASA resources to teach surface radiation, dose calculations, life-support systems, space weather, Mars communications, and growing plants in space. Historical data and game values are clearly separated: Curiosity/RAD informs a radiation calculation, while OSDR RadLab readings are labeled as measurements from the ISS, not Mars. SOL-3 turns mission-planning trade-offs into a replayable experience where young players can test strategies and learn from their consequences.
details:
SOL-3 is a browser-playable 2D outpost-management and exploration game for ages 7–12. The campaign spans three simulated Martian sols. Players move through the base, complete missions, diagnose equipment failures, and choose how to allocate power, oxygen, water, food, crop care, repairs, and crew shelter. A seeded operation changes the starting situation and which system may fail. Choices carry costs: a full repair uses more energy and a spare part, while a temporary fix preserves the part but reduces system output; prioritizing crop growth uses more water, and increasing water recovery raises power demand. During a solar alert, the crew’s choice changes simulated exposure and possible endings.

AURA, a scripted onboard guide, cinematic scenes, and an in-game science archive explain mission concepts in plain language. It also links NASA resources about DONKI, life-support systems, Mars relay communications, space crops, and PONDS. The current bundled data has no DONKI event records. The game labels historical measurements separately from simulated resources, risks, and outcomes.

SOL-3 is built with Phaser 3, TypeScript, and Vite, and published on GitHub Pages with keyboard and touch controls. OpenAI Codex assisted with research and source interpretation, data interpretation, coding and debugging, UI layout, and editing or translating some text. No AI/ML model runs in the game, and the NASA measurements were not AI-generated.
